listing installs is for sure the most convenient and effective way to find out the entire partner network
hack 1: use `ubiquityos_app_slug` against the search API for comments and then filter a `Set` of the orgs which it has appeared in
hack 2: install a secondary app to avoid exposing kernel' pk (guaranteed it seems partner's will have to do this anyway)

1. partner's will use the same app slug, if you mean forks/development then they'd change to their own app slug.
2. That is also an effective suggestion

To get a better picture of how over-assigned the contributor might be across multiple partners (eventually we'll have loads).
---
1. Global storage would enable us to track a userbase across all partners. The user object can be updated any time they are assigned an issue within the network and we can track with ease. This can serve us in hundreds of ways not just with this use-case.
2. Parse devpool json (better with all issues filled, theres a task for it) + search API for `username: pull_requests`, filter those that match devpool orgs.
3. Depending on the user' visibility settings you'll likely be able to do it with GraphQL API but I'm not as knowledgeable with that API, I use the official [GitHub GQL Explorer](https://docs.github.com/en/graphql/overview/explorer) to investigate when I need to.
---
`author:keyrxng is:pr` returns all of my PRs. It's trivial to match devpool json orgs to the orgs returned by this query.
`author:keyrxng is:pr -org:ubq-testing` this is how to exclude an org. (166 PRs returned by this lmao, only ~10-15 are not PRs into the Ubiquity ecosystem, I like that)

Whichever query you feel is most effective dude go for it.

ohh I was hoping that wasn't the case. You could use `author: <xx> is:pr` and do an org comparison that way instead otherwise @0x4007 or @gentlementlegen will approve the new config item.

Storage has it's own [branch](https://github.com/ubiquity/devpool-directory/tree/__STORAGE__).
This fn is trying to find assigned issues so
- using search API to get all PRs, then filter, then get the linked issue via GQL or PR body parsing
- using search API with `assignee:keyrxng is:issue`, then just filter is another but it doesn't take PRs into consideration (not sure if that's something we should consider in this context)
option two is probably best. (a lot of cases exist where a user is assigned to a task after it's closed as completed etc too which probably should be considered when filtering the results)
update the return type annotation of `getAssignedIssues` to include the `listfor` type that the fallback returns, making it a union of either search or list results

Usually it's better to use 
```ts
const AssignedIssueScope = {
  ORG: "org",
  REPO: "repo",
  NETWORK: "network"
} as const
```
over enums, they are debated to be a bad practice and TS themselves said they regret adding it into the language. It results in less performant JS (because enums don't exist in JS) and can be lost during runtime in libs are not built correctly
They both represent a simple object where `Enum` adds a burden that can be avoided but it's dev preference in this regard as it's a point of debate in the TS world.
